articles.title_orig: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on the sidelines of APEC, White House says
articles.title_zh: Trump, Xi and Putin plan an unprecedented joint meeting on the sidelines of APEC, White House says
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen , China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.
“President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People’s Republic of China and the president of the Russian Federation,” Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said in a call with reporters Friday night. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”
It is not anticipated that any sort of agreement will come from the trilateral meeting, according to a senior U.S. official, who described the session as an “entry point” and “the first conversation,” pointing to the reduction of nuclear arsenals as a key topic.
“We do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the senior U.S. official said about the issue of nuclear weapons.
Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads , according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
The three-way summit with Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin comes at a complicated moment in relations for the three countries.
Trump intends to discuss the Iran war with the two leaders, but not the war in Ukraine, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that discussions about the war in Ukraine are a separate “track” that China is not part of so it would not be “appropriate.”
Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers.
Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin , even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.
There is no bilateral with Putin scheduled, but the two leaders will appear at events and the trilateral meeting together, according to a senior U.S. official.
There are no plans for Trump to engage with North Korea during the trip, according to a senior U.S. official.
Separately, Elon Musk will be the only business leader who is part of the president’s delegation, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that other U.S. business leaders will attend the summit in their own capacity but there is no official U.S. business delegation.
Musk will not be part of any official meetings, according to a senior U.S. official.
Two senior U.S. officials said that they don’t think Trump will raise the espionage investigation focused on Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence agent who allegedly had a romantic relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, with China.
“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip. In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” a senior U.S. official said. “These are national security matters that we develop in the administration and interagency process, and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there.”
By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China’s growing clout and prestige.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signaling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they’re making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don’t like,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.
More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China’s argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia’s war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.
The trilateral meeting could undercut China’s push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism ,” he said.
Putin and Xi are no strangers. They’ve fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.”
Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the No. 1 trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.
As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia , China increased its purchases of Russia’s energy resources and became Moscow’s principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.
In the lead-up to Russia’s war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship.” China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv’s Western allies played a part in provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine .
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing’s policy on issues related to Taiwan.
Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.
Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which the leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalized plans for establishing the United Nations.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can’t be enforced on others.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia scandal hits Trump’s political vulnerabilities after Democratic sweep
articles.title_zh: Nvidia scandal hits Trump’s political vulnerabilities after Democratic sweep
articles.content_orig:
The scandal that brought down Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is now threatening one of President Donald Trump 's most influential Cabinet members—and could reshape the future of his signature tariff policies.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, a central architect and defender of Trump's trade agenda, is facing mounting pressure over his department's handling of restrictions on advanced American artificial intelligence chips reaching China .
The pressure is coming from inside the administration.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly pointed to Lutnick's department Friday, saying several major government agencies had supported blacklisting a Singapore-based company at the center of the Nvidia scandal for months, but that Commerce had the final say.
"Treasury, War, USTR, and State, they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months," Bessent said on CNBC's Squawk Box .
"But Commerce has the pen, Commerce BIS has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes."
The remarks came a day after Reuters reported that senior White House officials were discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, citing two people familiar with the situation.
Lutnick's departure would also have implications far beyond the Nvidia controversy. It could shift influence over Trump's tariffs toward U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, potentially opening the door to agreements that reduce duties on imports from major American trading partners.
But it could also have the opposite effect.
"Lutnick is part of the team that developed Trump's tariff strategy and has responsibility for the implementation of the tariff policy," Jeffrey Schott, a senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told Newsweek Saturday.
"His departure would not necessarily weaken the current policy because his replacement might implement the policy more forcefully."
The uncertainty comes as lawmakers in both parties question aspects of Trump's trade agenda and Democrats prepare to take control of Congress following last week's midterm elections.
Newsweek has reached out to the White House and the Commerce Department for comment.
Huang resigned Thursday after 33 years leading Nvidia , following revelations about extramarital relationships, including one involving a Chinese businesswoman suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of working for Beijing.
The scandal began with reports that Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's advanced AI chips.
U.S. intelligence officials suspected Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia founder, had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather intelligence and potentially influence Nvidia's advocacy for greater Chinese access to American technology, according to The New York Times .
China has rejected the espionage allegations as unsubstantiated. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.
Nvidia's board said last weekend that it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets had been compromised.
Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not publicly identify the person involved.
The controversy intensified Wednesday when the Times reported a second relationship, this time with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare , who reported directly to him.
The reports threw Huang's future at Nvidia into doubt before the board accepted his resignation.
A third relationship , involving another Nvidia employee, was reported by Reuters on Thursday, after his resignation.
The scandal has prompted congressional scrutiny not only of Nvidia but also of the Trump administration 's handling of chip exports to China.
Republican Senator Tim Scott, chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, has requested that Huang testify December 3 and Lutnick December 10 over national security concerns involving the chipmaker. A Lutnick spokesperson said the commerce secretary had agreed to testify voluntarily, according to CNBC.
Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana has also demanded answers.
"Secretary Lutnick needs to answer that in front of God and country," Kennedy told Politico on Wednesday.
Asked Thursday whether Lutnick should lose his job, Kennedy told CNN: "I don't know yet."
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons have meanwhile demanded that the administration preserve documents relating to Nvidia's exports to China and potential national security risks.
The controversy has intensified questions about why the Commerce Department has not added new companies to a key U.S. trade blacklist since October 2025, the longest gap between additions in more than a decade, according to Reuters.
Nvidia has appointed longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent replacement.
Trump has already endorsed former Apple CEO Tim Cook for the position, writing Thursday on Truth Social: "A Legend replaces a Legend!"
Dan Ives, a technology analyst and partner at Yorkville Ives & Co., told Newsweek that Cook was the top candidate .
The leadership upheaval has rattled investors. Nvidia shares plunged about 14 percent early Thursday before recovering much of the loss and closing down 4.3 percent. The stock fell another 2 percent Friday, bringing its two-day decline to about 6.3 percent.
Ives cut his price target for Nvidia from $300 to $225 after Huang's departure, reflecting the potential loss of what Newsweek described as the co-founder's $1.8 trillion leadership premium .
The company's influence in Washington could also suffer.
Chris Miller, a Tufts University associate professor and author of Chip War , told Newsweek that the scandal would substantially reduce Nvidia's influence over U.S. technology policy toward China.
Huang had cultivated a close relationship with Trump, becoming a prominent advocate for easing restrictions on American AI chip sales to China.
He visited the White House, traveled aboard Air Force One and personally lobbied the president to allow Nvidia to expand its business in the Chinese market.
Trump supported Huang even after the allegations involving Alice Huang emerged.
"I just think he's a very honorable man," Trump told reporters Monday, adding that the Nvidia executive had assured him he did not know the woman was a suspected spy.
The controversy has also drawn attention to the Trump administration's decisions on advanced chip exports to China.
In December 2025, Trump agreed to allow Nvidia to sell advanced H200 AI chips to approved customers in China under an arrangement that would give the U.S. government a share of the export revenue.
That decision has drawn criticism from lawmakers concerned that advanced American technology could strengthen China's military and intelligence capabilities.
Democratic Senator Ron Wyden and Representative Richard Neal have launched an investigation into the arrangement, questioning whether the government's share of export sales amounts to an "unconstitutional export tax."
The history of Huang's lobbying and dealings involving China has come under renewed scrutiny since the espionage allegations became public.
Lutnick's role has also attracted attention.
The New York Times reported Thursday that Lutnick frequently communicated with Huang and that his department gave Nvidia unusual access to its policymaking process.
According to the newspaper, Lutnick resisted or delayed efforts by other administration officials to tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to China.
The Washington Post reported Friday that a former administration official said Trump had repeatedly directed Lutnick to tighten restrictions on Nvidia's most powerful chips, but that Lutnick resisted because he feared provoking a trade war with China.
Treasury Secretary Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Greer were among officials who favored tougher controls, the Times reported.

articles.title_orig: Live updates: SpaceX Starship soars in orbit, still aiming for ship catch in unprecedented test flight
articles.title_zh: Live updates: SpaceX Starship soars in orbit, still aiming for ship catch in unprecedented test flight
articles.content_orig:
In a key test flight on Friday, SpaceX tried but failed to recover both stages of its massive Starship rocket.
The rocket lifted off from the company's South Texas launch facility at 4:47 p.m. local time, or 5:47 p.m. ET. SpaceX had to abort its plans to catch and reuse the booster, instead diverting it to splash into the Gulf of Mexico, where it burst into flames.
Test Flight 15, the most ambitious Starship mission to date, was the first time Elon Musk's company attempted to catch both the booster and upper stage, or spacecraft portion, of the massive rocket.
Earlier on Friday, SpaceX obtained authorization from the Federal Aviation Administration. Hours later, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop after reporting communication problems affecting "multiple" air traffic control centers. The SpaceX license wasn't effected by the flight stoppage, a spokesperson for the FAA told CNBC.
The upper stage of the Starship continued its trajectory into orbit after the company failed to catch and salvage the booster. The rocket is expected to fly around the Earth fourteen times in total. If successful, SpaceX will land the upper stage back at its Starbase facility on Saturday.
Starship's success is critical to SpaceX and its ambitions to eventually lift cargo and people to the surface of the Moon and Mars. In the near-term, SpaceX needs to send more satellites into orbit to expands its Starlink satellite internet service, which is currently the company's profit center.
The company's constellation already includes over 11,000 active satellites in low Earth orbit. One Starship rocket has the capacity to carry up to 60 Starlink v3 satellites into orbit, the company has said, representing about 20 times the capacity of earlier Falcon 9 rockets.
In the previous Starship test flight, the company released 26 v3 satellites, and released another 26 in the Friday test flight, with the goal of "Starlink becoming 51% of the internet," SpaceX said in a post on X.
When it comes to launches, "SpaceX is likely a full decade ahead of peers on this front," William Blair analysts wrote in a note out on Friday. "Even if tonight's catch is unsuccessful, a delay by a few months is not that consequential."
Meanwhile, SpaceX is facing fresh criticism over restrictions imposed on its Starshield satellite internet service in Ukraine. Starshield is built on Starlink technology and is the military-tier of SpaceX's satellite internet service.
Earlier this week, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country's military forces had experienced limits on Starshield without warning again, harming their ability to defend against Russia's ongoing aerial attacks. Similar limits on Starshield in Ukraine were temporarily imposed last month .
Some U.S. senators have condemned the restrictions, and urged Congress to investigate SpaceX .

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: 3 oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: 3 oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
articles.content_orig:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Iran-backed Houthi militant group said it intercepted and destroyed two drones on Saturday.
The drones were intercepted near Riyadh and over the southern region. The coalition was not more specific about where in the south it had been intercepted. Riyadh, the country's capital, is located in central Saudi Arabia, though hundreds of miles from the Houthis' base of operations in Yemen.
It was a busy week of drone and missile interceptions by the Saudis. The two drones intercepted on Saturday afternoon were the first since one was fired at the eastern, oil-rich region of the country on Thursday. Multiple drones in the east and near Riyadh were interrupted Thursday, while two ballistic missiles were shot down on Wednesday in the western part of Saudi Arabia and three others were shot down near Riyadh, according to the coalition.
Two drones were also intercepted on Wednesday, the coalition said, though one destroyed near Mecca was disavowed by the Houthis, who have said they will not target the holy city.
Multiple drones, ballistic missiles and cruise missiles were also intercepted over different parts of Saudi Arabia on Monday, the same day the coalition said it took out a weapons manufacturing facility in Yemen.
Iran and the United States should "immediately" allow fertilizer shipments through the Strait of Hormuz to ease the crisis in some of the most vulnerable countries, a senior U.N. official said Saturday.
Jorge Moreira da Silva, head of the U.N. Office for Project Services, told the COP31 climate talks in the Turkish resort city of Antalya that the lack of fertilizers could push millions into poverty.
While Iran and the United States are still trying to negotiate an end to the conflict, Moreira da Silva said he had the same message for both countries.
"They should continue their negotiations about the comprehensive deal — but that deal should not avoid an immediate, exceptional, limited, and time-bound solution for the fertilizers," he said.
"Basically what we need is five vessels a day with fertilizers," he added.
Before the conflict, a third of the world's fertilizers passed through the Strait of Hormuz, and since the blockades, their prices had risen by 30%, Moreira da Silva said.
Sudan's finance minister recently told him the price of food there had doubled in six months, he added. In Nepal, they told him that farmers could no longer afford to buy fertilizers.
"So it's very important that we are aware that countries such as Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka are facing very significant impact," Moreira da Silva said.
The effects of this shortage could be catastrophic, he warned.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps claims to have shot down an American MQ-1 "Predator" drone for the second straight day on Saturday.
This was the 17th MQ-1 drone shot down by Iran, according to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, though that number was not possible to verify. The U.S. certainly has lost a number of the drones, however, either to them being shot down or crashing.
The drone was shot down over Iran's Qeshm Island, which is located along the northern coast of the Strait of Hormuz. Like Friday, the strike was credited to Iran's alleged new air defense system.
The U.S. has lost dozens of unmanned aircraft during the war with Iran, according to a congressional report dated Oct. 5. Forty-five MQ-9 Reaper drones have been lost, just through mid-August, while at least three Predator drones were previously destroyed, according to the report.
There were at least 81 manned or unmanned aircraft lost during the war in Iran through early October, according to the report. As of Aug. 1, the losses amounted to a cost of between $1.9 billion and $3.3 billion.
Iran's military said on Saturday that fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has insisted vessels obtain its authorization to cross the strait since war erupted with the United States in February, and has attacked ships that do not comply.
"A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorized route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement on the incident in the south of the waterway, carried by the Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday.
A separate statement from Iran's conventional navy said another tanker "navigating through the unsafe and prohibited zone east of the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking and identification systems switched off, caught fire and was forced to stop after striking a naval mine".
The statements did not provide the names or origins of the vessels but the Guards said one of those hit in south Hormuz was a supertanker.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Saturday that explosions rang out on two oil tankers after they struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has restricted navigation.
Since war erupted in February, Tehran has insisted that vessels obtain its authorization to cross the strait and has attacked ships that do not comply.
"A short while ago, two oil tankers that had switched off their radar and positioning systems and were secretly attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz through an unauthorized route exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine," the Guards' navy said in a statement carried by an Iranian state broadcaster early on Saturday.
The statement did not provide the names or origins of the vessels, but said one was a supertanker.
The U.S., in response to Tehran's choking of the strategic trade route, has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and provides military support to tankers using the waterway.
In recent weeks, Iran's armed forces have reported several fires or explosions on board ships in the strait, often saying the vessels had struck mines.
On Friday, the Guards released footage of a large plume of smoke rising from a vessel it said was carrying liquefied gas and hit a mine in the south of the strait.
The U.S. military, however, has said it has cleared the main routes through the waterway of mines .
U.N. deputy spokesman Farhan Haq said Friday that civilians across Yemen are increasingly being hit by drones, missiles, airstrikes and shelling in their homes, markets and other places once considered safe.
In one of the deadliest attacks since fighting resumed between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Saudi-backed government forces, at least 30 people died in airstrikes on a market in Taiz province on Nov. 6, according to the Houthis.
Under international law, Haq said all parties must take "all feasible precautions" to avoid and minimize the death and injury to civilians.
Oil prices swung a day after President Trump said the U.S. didn't "need a deal with Iran" even as the conflict in the Middle East drags on.
Brent crude, the international standard, initially jumped early Friday before easing. It was mostly unchanged at $95.89 a barrel at 2 p.m. ET. It was trading near $72 per barrel in late February before the Iran war began.
Rising energy prices because of the U.S. war with Iran have been fueling inflation. Household budgets are getting squeezed directly by higher gasoline costs, but pricier gas and diesel raise costs for anything that is shipped. Prices for everything from food to clothing have been rising.
The latest wholesale inflation report released Friday also shows food prices and other costs gaining ground, despite some easing for energy costs.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani signed a mutual defense agreement Friday in Istanbul, according to Erdogan's office.

articles.title_orig: Andy Burnham says UK has ‘lost more than we gained’ through Brexit
articles.title_zh: Andy Burnham says UK has ‘lost more than we gained’ through Brexit
articles.content_orig:
PM accuses Tories of burning ‘all our bridges’ and says deal he is pursuing with EU will ‘get food prices down’
Andy Burnham has said the UK has “lost more than we gained” since leaving the EU, the prime minister’s latest in a string of comments criticising Brexit.
Outlining his desire to form closer ties with Brussels, Burnham accused the Conservative party of having “burned all our bridges” with the bloc after Brexit and said a new deal he hopes to secure with the EU next week will “get food prices down” and put more money in the pockets of British exporters.
The prime minister is due to meet European leaders at a summit next week and secure agreements that he says could raise GDP by 0.4% – about £17bn – including on food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme. He will also “explore options” for a different long-term relationship with Brussels.
Speaking at the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday, Burnham said: “We need to be willing to take difficult decisions to get the cost of living down.
“It’s why, in a few days’ time, I will head to the next UK-EU summit and I will be working hard as we move towards it to get to a new deal on food and farming between the UK and the EU. Why am I doing that? Because I want to help Welsh businesses.
The prime minister added: “I think we’ve lost more than we’ve gained over the last 10 years, and, actually, I think the Conservatives gave Britain a harsher and harder Brexit than people thought they were getting when they voted in 2016, because they burned all of our bridges in the aftermath, with the EU, and so I’m going to lead as prime minister on this issue, and I’m going to go and try and get the best deal I can for Wales, for those here who could benefit, Welsh farmers, exporters of Welsh shellfish and Welsh lamb.”
Burnham has recently said he is open to rejoining the single market, customs union or to “go all the way” by rejoining the EU, but on Saturday he said voters would ultimately be “the boss” of any changes.
He reiterated his commitment to Labour’s manifesto “red lines” – which rule out returning to the customs union, single market or free movement. “People working together in unions, trade unions, but also unions of nations, and that’s what makes us who we are,” he told the conference.
“And, yes, working with the European Union , as I said, but at the same time respecting the red lines in our manifesto and respecting the referendum, the referendum result. So, that’s the spirit, everybody, that I will take forward.”
The government has already made several announcements that would tie the UK closer to Brussels. Earlier this month, the Guardian reported that the UK was prepared to spend up to £450m a year to give EU students discounted university tuition fees, if Brussels allowed Britain access to the Made in Europe industrial programme.
Earlier this week, Hamish Falconer, the cabinet minister in charge of EU talks, said Britain was willing to discuss paying towards infrastructure schemes in poorer parts of the EU in return for access to the European electricity market.
after newsletter promotion
Despite Burnham’s recent pro-EU comments, senior figures in Brussels have said they want to see the UK begin to start paying for access to the European schemes it says it wants access to.
The EU’s former Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier told the BBC last week: “There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market.”
Ursula von der Leyen, the president of the European Commission, and António Costa, who leads the European Council, will meet Burnham on 20 November in Brussels for a summit where deals on food and drink, carbon emissions and youth exchange could be signed.
Barnier said the UK could not rejoin the single market “à la carte”, when speaking to the BBC’s Laura Kuenssberg last Sunday, adding: “I said very, very often during these negotiations, the Brexit, there is no cherrypicking.”

articles.title_orig: A new 'Yalta'? Trump and Putin push for a meeting that Xi is wary of hosting
articles.title_zh: A new 'Yalta'? Trump and Putin push for a meeting that Xi is wary of hosting
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen , China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers.
“President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People’s Republic of China and the president of the Russian Federation,” Olivia Wales, a White House spokesperson, said in a call with reporters Friday night. “The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous.”
It is not anticipated that any sort of agreement will come from the trilateral meeting, according to a senior U.S. official, who described the session as an “entry point” and “the first conversation,” pointing to the reduction of nuclear arsenals as a key topic.
“We do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the senior U.S. official said about the issue of nuclear weapons.
Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads , according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.
The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China.
The three-way summit with Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin comes at a complicated moment in relations for the three countries.
Trump intends to discuss the Iran war with the two leaders, but not the war in Ukraine, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that discussions about the war in Ukraine are a separate “track” that China is not part of so it would not be “appropriate.”
Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers.
Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin , even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.
There is no bilateral with Putin scheduled, but the two leaders will appear at events and the trilateral meeting together, according to a senior U.S. official.
There are no plans for Trump to engage with North Korea during the trip, according to a senior U.S. official.
Separately, Elon Musk will be the only business leader who is part of the president’s delegation, according to a senior U.S. official, who noted that other U.S. business leaders will attend the summit in their own capacity but there is no official U.S. business delegation.
Musk will not be part of any official meetings, according to a senior U.S. official.
Two senior U.S. officials said that they don’t think Trump will raise the espionage investigation focused on Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese intelligence agent who allegedly had a romantic relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, with China.
“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip. In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” a senior U.S. official said. “These are national security matters that we develop in the administration and interagency process, and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there.”
By agreeing to host the meeting, Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China’s growing clout and prestige.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.
“I think the key for Putin was that this was very much about signaling a desire to talk to the president and talk to Chairman Xi in a way that suggests that they’re making decisions on Ukraine, which obviously the Ukrainians and the Europeans don’t like,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
The trilateral could very well overshadow the APEC summit. The summit, which is bringing 21 economies to Shenzhen, marks a big moment for China to show off its fast-growing, ultramodern coastal metropolis that transformed from a small fishing village into a global technology and economic hub in just a few decades.
More substantively, such a gathering could also muddy China’s argument that a Cold War mentality in the West was a contributing factor that led to Russia’s war on Ukraine and its pointed criticism that the U.S. has undermined international institutions and treaties with how it has executed its war against Iran.
The trilateral meeting could undercut China’s push to portray itself as a defender of free trade at APEC, said Hoo Tiang Boon, a professor of Chinese foreign policy at Nanyang Technological University.
“You sort of run counter to Chinese support of multilateralism ,” he said.
Putin and Xi are no strangers. They’ve fostered a close personal relationship, meeting more than 40 times since Xi became president in 2013 and addressing each other as “dear friend.”
Trump and Putin have met face-to-face on seven different occasions, most recently in Alaska in August 2025. Xi and Trump have held face-to-face talks on eight occasions, including a September state visit to Washington by Xi.
Beijing is the No. 1 trading partner for Moscow, a relationship that has strengthened since Putin sent troops into Ukraine in 2022.
As the EU and the West sought to economically isolate Russia , China increased its purchases of Russia’s energy resources and became Moscow’s principal supplier of key technologies, including high-tech components for Russian weapons industries. Beijing has ignored Western demands to cut those supplies.
In the lead-up to Russia’s war on Ukraine, Xi and Putin declared their countries had a “no-limits friendship.” China officially has said it is neutral on the conflict, while charging that Kyiv’s Western allies played a part in provoking Russia’s military action in Ukraine .
Moscow, in turn, has repeatedly declared its support for Beijing’s policy on issues related to Taiwan.
Trump recently struck a diesel deal with Russia, waiving sanctions against Moscow and allowing for the sale of millions of tons of the fuel. The U.S. leader has blamed surging energy prices on Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries. Analysts, however, say the rise in global crude prices is due mostly to the Iran war.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has expressed concern that the trilateral meeting could serve as a platform for discussing a possible Ukraine deal behind Kyiv’s back.
Planning for the summit has drawn comparisons to the Yalta Conference, the 1945 gathering at which the leaders of the U.S., Britain and the Soviet Union agreed to divide Germany and Berlin into four military occupation zones and finalized plans for establishing the United Nations.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has dismissed the Yalta comparisons, noting that any potential agreements reached in Shenzhen can’t be enforced on others.

articles.title_orig: Thousands turn out in Edinburgh to protest against AI data centres
articles.title_zh: Thousands turn out in Edinburgh to protest against AI data centres
articles.content_orig:
Thousands of people have joined a protest in Edinburgh against the building of large-scale AI data centres.
Demonstrators with placards - and some dressed in costume - assembled at the top of the Royal Mile before marching towards the Scottish Parliament.
The event comes at a time of widespread debate about the environmental impact of data centres and is part of a wave of protests across Europe.
The Scottish government will soon publish new planning guidance on data centres and said it was developing a strategy to maximise the "public benefit".
Innovation Minister Alyn Smith recently said data centres were "the whisky bonds of the AI sector".
However protesters made it clear they disagree - carrying slogans such as "AI data centres threaten humanity" and "AI data centres: costing the Earth".
Some attended to voice their opposition to plans for data centres in particular communities - including Cockenzie, East Lothian, and Larbert, Falkirk.
Kim Cairns, a campaigner for 'Say No To Chapelcross AI Data Centre', told BBC Scotland News her community was worried about noise, road closures and access problems during the construction phase.
She was also concerned about the noise the centre would generate when it was operational.
Kim said: "It's not going to enrich anybody's lives. For Chapelcross it's the sheer size of it, the amount of electricity it's going to need.
"At the moment it's green fields with sheep and cows in it. It's going to be a monstrosity on the environment.
"The air pollution, the light pollution - it's just not needed."
AI is seen by some as the most transformative technology ever made but others have warned there is chance that if the frightening pace of development continues it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.
Meanwhile, Scotland's data centre debate centres around the scale and impact of the sites themselves.
At the moment, the biggest data centre in Scotland is thought to be DataVita's site in Airdrie, North Lanarkshire, which has a capacity for 12MW.
But if one planned for Chapelcross, Dumfries and Galloway, goes ahead it will have a capacity of 1,000MW - making it one of the largest data centres in the world.
The Scottish Greens and campaign groups have called for a moratorium on large data centres, arguing they could undermine climate targets and place additional pressure on renewable energy supplies.
The innovation minister previously told BBC Scotland some of the discourse around the subject was "wild".
Smith said: "You'd think there wasn't a planning system at all.
"Comparing a really bad data centre in the middle of the Utah desert doesn't track through to what we're going to have in Scotland."
Friends of the Earth campaigner Kim Pratt believes the people of Scotland should have the final say on the building of data centres.
She said: "The way that these data centres are being proposed is going to make a lot of profit for big tech companies but they're going to have huge impacts for people in Scotland.
"These developments are so massive they're going to have national-level impacts -they're energy hungry developments.
"There would be a massive increase in our energy bills but also in terms of climate impact as well.
"The Scottish government is only taking a few months to consider these impacts - and these developments are so new, we don't know what all the impacts will be."
The Scottish government confirmed it would publish new planning guidance on data centres before the end of the year and was "developing a strategic approach to maximising the public benefit from data centres located in Scotland".
A spokesperson added: "Planning authorities are also now required to notify ministers of new data centre applications, with a new planning direction also mandating an Environmental Impact Assessment to be submitted during planning for all new data centres with a power capacity exceeding 50 megawatts."

articles.title_orig: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
articles.title_zh: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
articles.content_orig:
US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The Ukrainian president's comments come after US President Donald Trump's envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable.
Russia controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday.
He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow.
Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider.
Moscow has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.
Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.
Russia has now raised the stakes further. It has revived 2021 demands for Nato to halt any expansion in Russia's vicinity and to roll back military infrastructure from countries of central and eastern Europe that became Nato members following the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
The US and other Western nations dismissed these demands then - and Moscow invaded Ukraine a few months later.
However, questions of European security were on the agenda of the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week.
Russia has insisted it will not agree to cease fighting until a final peace deal is in place that would include territorial settlements as well as security arrangements.
In the comments, made on Friday but only released on Saturday, Zelensky said that the US proposal made him believe that "Nato is back on the agenda".
But he cautioned: "You have also heard Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation."
Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas.
Ceding the small portions of land Ukraine still controls there would be symbolically significant for Kyiv.
Zelensky has previously spoken of retaking Russian-controlled territory in four of Ukraine's regions, as well as the Crimean peninsula, which Moscow annexed in 2014.
The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices.
Zelensky then accused US officials of limiting Ukraine's Starlink internet service , which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trump said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" and called for fresh elections.
Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership.

SpaceX succesfully launched its Starship Flight 15 mission on Friday, Nov. 13 , at 5:47 p.m. EDT (2247 GMT) from Starbase, Texas. Starship Flight 15 will attempt to land its Ship upper stage for the first time, but did abort a landing pad catch of its Super Heavy Booster. It will be the first-ever recovery of an orbital Starship upper stage, if successful. See launch video above and live views from SpaceX .
Follow our Starship Flight 15 coverage here as SpaceX completes its final prelaunch work for the launch, which also deployed 26 new Starlink V3 satellites into orbit.
Flight 15 landing livestream | Flight 15 launch video | SpaceX | Starship
Starship Die Cast Rocket Model Was $47.99 Now $39.99 on Amazon .
Even if you can't see SpaceX's Starship in person, you can score a model of your own. Standing at 13.77 inches (35 cm), this is a 1:375 ratio of SpaceX's Starship as a desktop model. The materials here are alloy steel and it weighs just 225g.
We just got some updated information about Super Heavy's landing abort during Starship Flight 15. SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot initially said that the booster diverted away from a "chopsticks" catch attempt at Starbase on Friday (Nov. 13) due to a guidance, navigation and control (GNC) issue. This morning (Nov. 14), however, he exonerated the GNC system, saying it performed as expected during Super Heavy's return to Earth.
The GNC system "detected that the booster was not in the place that it was supposed to be to proceed with a catch, did an automated abort and then headed out to that offshore splashdown location," Huot said. "The team's still digging into the root cause on how we got there, and so, more to come on that."
You can read our story about Super Heavy's landing abort here .
SpaceX is still planning to catch Starship's Ship upper stage at Starbase today. Everything looks good for that unprecedented attempt, which will occur at around 4:16 p.m. EST (2116 GMT), if all goes according to plan. You can watch it live here at Space.com.
We are now 16 hours into SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 mission , with just over six more hours remaining until the Ship 42 upper stage makes its attempted landing catch back at Starbase.
In an earlier post, I discussed SpaceX's update on how a guidance system issue caused the Super Heavy booster landing abort just after liftoff. You can now read my full story on the Super Heavy landing abort here .
Space.com's Josh Dinner captured the moment the Super Heavy booster triggered its flight termination system to explode in the Gulf of Mexico offshore from Starbase. Check it out.
Until the landing abort, the Starship Super Heavy booster performed as expected during its liftoff and stage separation, delivering its Ship upper stage to the proper position to fire its own engines and reach orbit.
Here's a stunning look at all 33 Super Heavy Raptor engines firing in unison to power the 41-story rocket's ascent into orbit, as seen by Josh.
The next Flight 15 milestone for SpaceX will be a "Final Hawaii Return Check" at the 20-hours, 41-minute mark of the mission. That will be a go/no-go moment when SpaceX decides whether to attempt the Starbase chopsticks landing at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT) for Ship 42, or direct it to a splashdown off the coast of Hawaii.
Our landing livestream will begin at about that check in time, at 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT).
Good morning and happy Saturday, Space Fans! Today is Flight Day 2 for SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight and SpaceX reports that its Ship 42 spacecraft is in good health as we near the 14-hour mark of its 22.5-hour test flight.
About 7 hours into the mission, SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot confirmed that flight controllers gave the go-ahead to forgo an early return window for a splashdown off the coast of Chile and proceed for the full 14-orbit flight. Starship is on track for a landing attempt, its first-ever from orbit, today (Nov. 14) at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT) . Space.com's livestream of SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 landing will begin at 2 p.m. EST and you can see it at the top of this page.
"Starship's going to stay in space. We are one step closer to an eventual return to launch site," Huot said in the update. "So that's great news."
Huot also reported that Starship's tile-covered heat shield appears in good shape for today's landing attempt. SpaceX used long-range ground-based cameras and cameras on some of the 26 Starlink satellites the Ship deployed to check its heat shield after liftoff.
"Our heat shield team reviewed all the data we got from our ground tracking cameras, and from those satellite cameras and confirmed the heat shield is in a good posture for a reentry and return to the launch site," Huot said.
Huot also said it was likely a guidance and navigation control issue that caused the Booster 22 Super Heavy first stage to abort its landing attempt after liftoff on Friday. The giant booster plunged into the Gulf of Mexico instead of making a landing patch catch at Starbase, Texas.
The next "early return" check will come about 20 hours into the mission, around 2 p.m. EST (1900 GMT), when flight controllers will have to decide for hte last time whether to press ahead with the landing attempt or send Starship to a splashdown off the coast of Hawaii.
SpaceX's Starship spacecraft Ship 42 is flying over Southeast Asia and the Indian Ocean as it continues its long coast 260 kilometers above Earth.
You can actually try to spot Starship in the night sky using our guide here .
SpaceX's livestream is showing the position of the spacecraft, giving you an idea of where and when to look. You should be fast though, as Starship is moving at about 26,442 km/hour.
If you do see Starship in the night sky, let us know! Send us a note on what you saw and your photos here: spacephotos@space.com.
SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 Ship vehicle has successfully deployed all 26 Starlink satellites and has now entered an extended coast phase of its mission that should last well into tomorrow. Here's our launch wrap with video and photos from Josh Dinner at the launch site.
The Ship 42 spacecraft deployed all 26 Starlink V3 internet satellites by the 1-hour, 17-minute mark of the mission.
Flight controllers then decided to forgo an "early return" option to land Starship early with an ocean splashdown off the coast of Hawaii. The option, at the 90-minute mark of the flight, is the first of three "early return" options fopr Starship in case something goes wrong.
So far, Ship 42 is performing well in orbit. The next early-return checkpoint is about 7.5 hours into the mission, which will occur around 1 a.m. EST (0600 GMT).
"That means this is now going to be the longest Starship mission we've ever flown," SpaceX's Dan Huot said. "We're going to surpass the point that we had to come home on Flight 14. So that's already exciting."
Huot and other SpaceX commentators will return in a few hours with a status update. So for now, Starship is just coasting in space.
It's been one hour since SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launch and Starlink satellite deployment is underway.
So far, the Ship 42 upper stage has deployed 12 of 26 Starlink V3 internet satellites, with more popping out of its Pez-dispenser like payload bay every few minutes.

articles.title_orig: Tesla Opens Sales of Autonomous Cybercab for ‘Select’ Customers
articles.title_zh: Tesla Opens Sales of Autonomous Cybercab for ‘Select’ Customers
articles.content_orig:
Tesla’s long-promised Cybercab is finally available for personal purchase, at least for a select few in the Austin area. But it’s far from a straightforward ownership experience.
The $29,990 price tag comes with a stack of restrictions that redefine what “owning” the vehicle actually means. The two-seat, steering-wheel-free Robotaxi, previously limited to Tesla’s own fleet, now carries contractual terms that limit where it can go, how it can be used, and whether it can even move without an active paid subscription.
Late on November 13 , Tesla announced that select customers were being invited to order a Cybercab for personal use.
Tesla Cybercab goes on sale for $29,990, slated for December deliveries
The estimated purchase price is $29,990 before taxes, paired with a non-refundable $1,000 deposit and an estimated December 2026 delivery in Austin, Texas. The first month of the required :Autonomy Subscription,” priced at $299 per month is included.
After that, the vehicle needs an active subscription to operate at all. The announcement confirmed that customer sales had begun, albeit on an invite-only basis rather than a public order page.
BREAKING: Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription terms are now live. A paid monthly subscription is required. 1/12 Tesla: “Your Cybercab will not operate without an active Autonomy Subscription. 🧵 https://t.co/umVk6DJE2x
— Spencer (@scotsrule08) November 13, 2026
For those invited to order, the agreements (Cybercab Order Agreement, Terms of Use, and Autonomy Subscription Agreement) impose significant constraints. Major points include:
Tesla’s approach prioritizes control over a vehicle designed without traditional human controls and intended primarily as transport-as-a-service, something that Musk has hinted toward for some time now. Restricting commercial use and modifications could be as much of a software integrity, safety, and data collection effort as it is a safety effort.
Fleet consistency could also be in regulatory scrutiny early on in the Cybercab’s days of public operation.
The subscription model generates ongoing revenue beyond the low vehicle price and ensures the car remains connected and updatable, something that will keep the Cybercab as safe as possible as new updates roll out.
Buyback and resale limits reduce the risk of vehicles circulating outside Tesla’s operational and service ecosystem.
It apperas that personal ownership is secondary to the broader Robotaxi network strategy , as Musk has previously stated that the vast majority of Cybercabs would remain Tesla-owned.
Initial deliveries are estimated for Austin, but personal vehicles are able to operate in any of Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences:
It’ll work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as @robotaxi, just serving the owners’ needs.
— Ashok Elluswamy (@aelluswamy) November 14, 2026
Those who have been invited to order can also have their personal Cybercab delivered to numerous locations in Texas, including:
Interesting that you can choose a delivery city https://t.co/SknDz9rFzo
— Whole Mars Catalog (@wholemars) November 14, 2026
As far as the monthly “Autonomy Subscription,” it appears Musk already wants it to be low. He acknowledged last night on X that the subscription price is too high. Along with detailing that the Cybercab will be available nationwide as regulatory approval is received, Musk said the monthly fee should match the cost of FSD and Premium Connectivity, which is about $115 per month.
The launch marks a milestone for unsupervised personal autonomous vehicles, but the fine print makes clear that buyers are purchasing a highly constrained asset whose usefulness is tightly bound to Tesla’s software, service network, and geographic approvals.

Tesla has officially put the Cybercab up for sale, revealing a bargain price and a $299 per month “Autonomy Subscription” that could hit customer hands as soon as December.
The offer requires a $299 monthly Autonomy Subscription, with the first month included in the purchase price, along with a $1,000 non-refundable order deposit. Tesla’s ordering interface shows deliveries targeted for Austin, Texas.
Tesla says that the Cybercab is making transportation more efficient, affordable and accessible than ever before, and that buyers can order their own Cybercab for personal use.
🚨🚨🚨 BREAKING: Tesla Cybercab is officially on sale for $29,990 with a $299/mo “Autonomy Subscription”
Delivery slotted for December! HUGE!
— TESLARATI (@Teslarati) November 13, 2026
The Cybercab is Tesla’s dedicated robotaxi, a gold-finished, two-passenger vehicle without a steering wheel or pedals, designed from the outset for unsupervised autonomous operation. It has been in limited Robotaxi service in Austin since September 2026 , operating alongside Tesla’s larger fleet of Model Y vehicles.
Production takes place at Gigafactory Texas, which launched earlier this year. Tesla has stated for some time that it planned to put Cybercabs on sale by the end of the year, and it looks like they will come through on that promise if everything goes according to plan.
The Autonomy Subscription is mandatory for the vehicle to operate because it is void of a steering wheel and pedals . Tesla notes that the subscription and regular vehicle maintenance are required, indicating that personal owners will depend on the company’s software and service infrastructure rather than traditional ownership models.
One month of the subscription is included with purchase and subsequent months are billed separately until canceled.
This limited personal-sales opening marks a shift from Tesla’s earlier emphasis on fleet and transport-as-a-service operations. During the Q3 2026 Earnings Call, executives indicated that the vast majority of Cybercabs would remain Tesla-owned and used for rideshare service, while still aiming to place some vehicles with customers by year-end.
Elon Musk has previously targeted a price below $30,000, which was a h uge point of emphasis for the Cybercab being the central point of Tesla’s “transportation-as-a-service” model.
Availability remains restricted to invited customers rather than a public order page, and the initial deliveries are expected only in the Austin area where unsupervised Robotaxi operations are already active. Buyers will need to accept the geographic and operational constraints of current autonomous deployment, as the vehicle cannot be driven manually outside supported zones.
The move gives a small number of early buyers the chance to own Tesla’s dedicated autonomous vehicle at the long-discussed sub-$30,000 price point, while the bulk of production continues to support the company’s expanding Robotaxi network.

articles.title_orig: How the Nvidia scandal lifted the curtain on a loophole that’s giving China access to US chips
articles.title_zh: How the Nvidia scandal lifted the curtain on a loophole that’s giving China access to US chips
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump is not expected to raise allegations of a Chinese intelligence operation involving former Nvidia CEO J ensen Huang during his upcoming meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, senior U.S. officials said Friday.
Officials also said that Elon Musk , the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, will accompany Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.
The White House, earlier Friday, said Trump plans to have a three-way summit there with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Jensen Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, who is not related to him, has raised concerns that a Singapore-based company where she was an executive diverted restricted Nvidia chips to China.
"The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip," an official said on the press call, speaking on the condition that they not be identified.
"In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls ... and we don't expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we're there."
Asked if Trump would raise the allegations against Alice Huang to Chinese leader Xi Jinping, the official said, "The focus of a meeting with President Xi, at least on the economic side, is going to be about implementation of the trade agreement."
"When it comes to some of these national security matters and examinations and investigations that are going on in the U.S., [that is] probably not something that we're going to read the Chinese in on at this moment," the official said.
Another official said, "I don't expect the president to raise it — the Alice Huang issue."
China has called the allegations against Alice Huang baseless.
Huang resigned this week as Nvidia's CEO after damning reports that he had an affair with Alice Huang, who was an executive of Megaspeed , a cloud-computing company that is being eyed for possible facilitation of sending billions of dollars worth of Nvidia chips in violation of U.S. restrictions on those chips.
The scandal has rocked Nvidia and raised questions about whether the Commerce Department, which is led by Howard Lutnick, has been aggressive enough at blocking advanced chips from ending up in China.
During Friday's call, a reporter asked why Musk was going on the trip with Trump.
"I don't want to speak for the president on exactly why Elon's going," an official said.
"Obviously, he has tremendous business interests in the U.S.-China relationship. He's a big part of our national security," the official said. "There are numerous reasons, given the engagement that the president is going to have, where I think Elon would be of tremendous benefit, just even as an advisor to the president."

articles.title_orig: Driver Stops in Front of Moving Car, Then Gets Mad When Motorist Goes Around: "Road Rage Or Insurance Scam?"
articles.title_zh: Driver Stops in Front of Moving Car, Then Gets Mad When Motorist Goes Around: "Road Rage Or Insurance Scam?"
articles.content_orig:
A driver traveling on a rain-soaked road had to stop suddenly when another motorist moved into their lane and slammed on the brakes. The close call was only the start of an encounter that soon drew thousands of reactions online.
Dashcam footage shared on Reddit on November 8 shows the confrontation on a suburban road. According to the person who posted the video, the other driver came to a complete stop, leaving little room to get around.
The motorist said the other driver began yelling and making rude gestures before following their vehicle. What started as a possible rear-end crash had turned into a confrontation that continued even after the cars separated.
Now, people watching the clip are arguing over what caused the strange behavior. Some suspect road rage, while others think the driver may have been trying to cause a crash for an insurance claim.
The original Reddit post , shared by u/pooh_jo in r/dashcams, describes a drive that took an unexpected turn.
The recording begins on a wet suburban road, with other vehicles traveling nearby. As the dashcam vehicle moves forward, another car enters its lane and slows sharply before coming to a stop.
The driver behind manages to avoid hitting it, but getting past is another problem. According to the person who posted the footage, they had to reverse before there was enough space to drive around the stopped vehicle.
Rather than simply continuing down the road, the other motorist reportedly became angry. The person behind the dashcam described the driver yelling, making an obscene gesture, and later flashing their headlights while following.
The person who posted the video could not explain why the other motorist behaved that way. In the original description, they wrote, "I have no idea if this was some sort of road rage or insurance scam."
That question quickly took over the comments. One Reddit user wrote, "Honestly seems like an Insurance scam." Others agreed, pointing to the wet pavement and sudden stop as reasons for concern.
Not everyone accepted that explanation. Some commenters thought the driver might have been upset about the dashcam vehicle's speed and was trying to force it to slow down.
Another viewer suggested that a person planning an insurance scam would likely have driven away once the attempted collision failed. The continued confrontation, in that user's view, looked more like someone trying to make a point.
Neither explanation has been established. The post contains no evidence of an insurance claim or a confirmed motive for the other driver's actions.
The discussion also turned toward the person recording the footage. Several commenters questioned whether the dashcam driver was traveling too quickly for the rainy conditions.
Others pushed back, arguing that the vehicle appeared to leave enough room for nearby traffic and that the driver responded carefully to the sudden stop. One commenter claimed the posted speed was only slightly above the road's limit, though that limit has not been independently confirmed.
The argument soon shifted from the dashcam vehicle's speed to whether either driver had the right to confront another motorist over their driving.
One commenter put it simply: "Explanation doesn't equal excuse."
The person who shared the footage did not report a collision in their description. Instead, they described escaping the stopped vehicle only to have the other driver flash their lights and follow afterward.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang had a strict meetings rule for his 60 reports—Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang had a strict meetings rule for his 60 reports—Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra
articles.content_orig:
Former Nvidia CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang famously avoided unnecessary meetings, prioritizing efficiency over routine check-ins. Even with, at one point, 60 direct reports , he refused to do catch-ups. Now that he’s resigned , the question is whether his successor (currently Colette Kress who has stepped up on an interim basis) will keep the rule.
Speaking at Stanford University , Huang once disclosed his aversion to frequent catch-ups. “I don’t do one-on-ones with any of them,” he said.
Huang argued frequent meetings would clutter his schedule. He said they would also get in the way of the broader team’s ability to address challenges, work effectively, and stay transparent.
“They never hear me say something to them, that is only for them to know,” he said. “There’s not one piece of information that I somehow secretly tell the staff; I don’t tell the rest of the company.”
“In that way, our company was designed for agility. For information to be to flow as quickly as possible. For people to be empowered by what they are able to do, not what they know,” he added.
But that doesn’t mean he had no time for his team. Huang insisted he still regularly caught up with his executives. They just didn’t need to set time aside in their diaries to be on the same page.
“I write no reviews for any of them,” he added. “I give them constant reviews and they provide the same to me.”
And when an employee genuinely needed a moment of his time, Huang insisted he’d “drop everything for them.”
Stepping into Huang’s shoes (for now) is CFO Colette Kress . The interim CEO, who has an estimated net worth of $1.2 billion according to Forbes , holds a bachelor’s in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.
After nearly three decades’ worth of financial roles at companies such as Texas Instruments , Cisco, and Microsoft , she joined Nvidia in September 2013.
Since then, she guided the company’s finances through a significant transformation, from a business largely focused on video game hardware to a chipmaking powerhouse at the center of the AI boom—and watched its market cap soar from about $9 billion to, at its peak, $5 trillion. Its since dropped below $4 trillion upon the news regarding Huang.
She hasn’t revealed whether she’ll ditch one-on-ones too. But the 59-year-old, who has spent 13 years as Huang’s right hand on Nvidia’s finances, seems to share his affinity for efficiency.
“We do not waste a day, we don’t waste a dime,” Kress said in 2024. “And those two things are really important about us, our agility to move fast, but our ability to not waste things along the way.”
Huang isn’t the first leader to argue that meetings aren’t the best use of time.
Pandora’s former CEO Alexander Lacik told Fortune too many meetings result in every department or company issue getting “equal attention”—whether or not it needs it. He limited his catch-ups with management.
“There’s only one, two, three activities that actually draw disproportionate value and the rest is just background noise,” he said. “As time has gone by and I’m getting towards the end of my career, I’m much more clear on trying to insert myself where I make a high impact.”
United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby caps his meetings at four hours a day , and wants the ones he does attend to be “quick” and “almost all conversational.”
E-commerce giant Shopify took one step further and actually axed all meetings involving more than two people in 2023, in a company-wide “calendar purge” meant to give employees more time to work on other tasks.
And even Amazon founder Jeff Bezos—a big fan of “ messy meetings ”—mandates a strict protocol to ensure they’re actually useful, complete with a six-page memo instead of a PowerPoint (because they’re too vague) and half an hour set aside at the start of the meeting to silently read it together before having “a really elevated discussion.”
A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on June 12, 2024.
Orianna Rosa Royle is the Success associate editor at Fortune , overseeing careers, leadership, and company culture coverage. She was previously the senior reporter at Management Today , Britain's longest-running publication for CEOs.

articles.title_orig: Nearly €20m in cash found buried, hidden in Hungary corruption case
articles.title_zh: Nearly €20m in cash found buried, hidden in Hungary corruption case
articles.content_orig:
Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly €20 million in cash buried in forests, hidden in warehouses and residential properties and stored in a high-value safe as part of a bribery investigation into a former minister.
The money was found during searches on Thursday and Friday as part of a criminal investigation into former minister Miklós Seszták, who worked under former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, relating to bribery allegations. ​Seszták, who is under pre-trial detention has denied wrongdoing.
Hungarian Prime Minister Peter ‌Magyar launched a wide anti-corruption campaign after ousting Orbán earlier this year.
The money — more than 5 billion forints, €2.6 million and €1.2 million — was found across locations in Budapest, Pest, Békés and Nógrád counties, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office, an anti-corruption body, said in a statement .
“This officially marks the end for the Fidesz-KDNP mafia!” Magyar posted on Facebook , originally in Hungarian, in reference to Orbán’s government.
It took 12 Treasury staff eight hours to tally the cash using 5 counting machines, Finance Minister Kármán András said.
The announcement comes after Hungarian authorities detained Aron Orbán, the former prime minister’s brother, as part of an investigation into people smuggling. The former prime minister said on social media that the move, announced by Magyar on Monday, was part of a “political witch-hunt” to get him.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk reacted wryly to the latest announcement, referring to the arrest of Orbán’s brother and the cash discovery on X .
“Dear Victor, I’ve always been an admirer of your creativity, but now I must say I’m impressed as never before,” he wrote.

articles.title_orig: AT&T begins shutting down landline services in Middle Tennessee this weekend, here's what to know
articles.title_zh: AT&T begins shutting down landline services in Middle Tennessee this weekend, here's what to know
articles.content_orig:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WTVF) — Starting this Sunday, AT&T will begin shutting down landline services across several Middle Tennessee communities after receiving permission from the Federal Communications Commission.
While the change may not affect everyone directly, experts say homeowners and business owners should know a few key things before the service disappears.
You're talking about fax lines, security lines, elevator lines — especially when it comes to condos, townhomes, business centers, medical plazas. That's where you're going to see the vast majority of them," said Stephen Burton from One Call Technology in Franklin.
The team at One Call Technology is already helping businesses prepare for the day their phone provider pulls the plug — a day that is quickly approaching.
"Different carriers are shutting off at different times, but people don't think it applies to them necessarily yet," said Burton.
An AT&T filing with the FCC shows the company plans to begin discontinuing service this weekend from dozens of wire centers across Tennessee. AT&T has until 2029 to complete the full transition.
For anyone with safety systems like fire alarms and emergency phones, experts say it's time to act now—before those systems stop working.
Navigating the changes does not have to be overwhelming.
"Reach out to a company. There are a lot in the Middle Tennessee area that you can talk with who are well aware of what's going on and can hold your hand and walk you through it," said Burton.
Something else to keep an eye on is what you're paying for older services going forward.
With pricing regulations no longer in place, some customers have seen the cost of their copper-based services climb dramatically.

articles.title_orig: Italy fines Meta $887 million over Android users' data access
articles.title_zh: Italy fines Meta $887 million over Android users' data access
articles.content_orig:
Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta €805m (£670; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent.
Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.
It has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately.
The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant.
The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts.
Facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in their gallery.
The regulator said it took into account "the high number of people affected" and the fact it is "still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system".
It also cited "Meta's lack of co-operation".
The BBC has reached out to Meta for comment.
Last month, Meta, which is also behind Instagram and WhatsApp, was hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices.
A US judge in New Mexico ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) after it found that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

articles.title_orig: Apple users are about to lose something they’ve had for 28 years
